Going through a custody battle, especially when emotional abuse is involved, is incredibly stressful. Whether your child's therapist can testify depends on your local laws, the therapist's professional guidelines, and the consent agreements you signed. Many therapists have strict policies against testifying in custody disputes because sharing session details can break the child's trust and damage the safe space they need for healing. Instead of the treating therapist, courts often rely on a specialized custody evaluator or a Guardian ad Litem to assess the situation. 

Because I cannot provide legal advice, it is very important to consult with a family law attorney who can guide you on the best way to legally present evidence of emotional abuse in your jurisdiction. You may also want to have an open conversation with the therapist about their boundaries regarding court involvement, so you know exactly what to expect and how best to support your child through this difficult process.
